# Phase 6: Polish, Consent Gate, Evaluation & Submission - Context

**Gathered:** 2026-10-08
**Status:** Ready for planning

<domain>
## Phase Boundary

Phase 6 hardens the user experience and prepares Treads for production release and hackathon submission. This includes full-screen versioned consent gate enforcement (`CONS-01`, `CONS-02`, `CONS-03`, `CONS-04`), progressive Tegaki handwriting reveals with web font fallback (`DSGN-03`), synthesized Cuelume Web Audio chimes and native haptics (`DSGN-04`, `DSGN-05`), batch evaluation benchmark execution and CLI assertion (`EVAL-01`), dead-code remediation with `fallow`, production build verification, and outdoor field walkthrough documentation.

</domain>

<decisions>
## Implementation Decisions

### Tegaki Handwriting Animation (DSGN-03)
- **D-01:** SVG path stroke dashoffset / cursive draw — Organic pen stroke drawing effect revealing handwritten letter paths progressively over ~1.2s.
- **D-02:** Accessible font fallback & reduced motion — Google Font Caveat cursive fallback with instant opacity reveal when `prefers-reduced-motion` is active.
- **D-03:** Strategic lifecycle placement — Animated on Landing hero headline and Entry Fact Card confirmed specimen titles; plays once on view entrance without re-animating on incidental re-renders.
- **D-04:** Dynamic text rendering — SVG text stroke with dashoffset reveal combined with Google Font Caveat cursive styling to scale seamlessly to arbitrary Latin and binomial species names from Wikipedia.

### Cuelume Synthesized Audio & Haptics (DSGN-04, DSGN-05)
- **D-05:** Organic acoustic synthesis — Dual-sine / triangle warm chime with exponential decay envelope (gentle brass/field bell character) using native Web Audio oscillators without external audio assets.
- **D-06:** Dual chime interaction mapping — Specimen confirmation triggers a warm major-third dual chime (E5–G#5); Daily Hunt completion triggers a joyful 4-note ascending arpeggio (C5–E5–G5–C6).
- **D-07:** Native tactile vibration pair — Crisp single tap [25ms] on capture/candidate selection, and resonant double pulse [40ms, 60ms, 80ms] on confirmation and daily hunt completion via `navigator.vibrate`.
- **D-08:** AudioContext lifecycle & preferences — Audio chimes defaulted to OFF; haptics defaulted to ON; lazy `AudioContext` resume on first user interaction to comply with mobile browser autoplay policies; configurable via `/settings`.

### Consent Gate Enforcement (CONS-01 to CONS-04)
- **D-09:** App-wide blocking modal overlay — Strict full-screen modal on first visit; blocks interaction until accepted, storing version in IndexedDB and calling `navigator.storage.persist()`. — **Reversibility:** costly — gates user entry flow across all routes.
- **D-10:** Semver versioning & revocation — Semver string (`"1.0.0"`) and ISO timestamp stored in `db.settings`; re-prompts only on breaking policy bumps; revocable via Danger Zone reset in `/settings`. — **Reversibility:** costly — defines database settings schema and migration behavior.
- **D-11:** Non-blocking permission fallbacks — Non-blocking inline banner with helpful guidance + immediate manual fallback (e.g. file picker for photo, manual text note for voice) when hardware permissions are denied.
- **D-12:** Persistent storage status reporting — Silent request on consent acceptance; live status badge in `/settings` ('Durable / Best-effort') with a one-tap retry button.

### Evaluation Harness & Field Polish (EVAL-01, Submission)
- **D-13:** Dual evaluation runner — Interactive visual dashboard on `/eval` + headless CLI test script (`scripts/run-eval-suite.ts` / `pnpm test:eval`) asserting ≥70% accuracy and ≥90% refusal.
- **D-14:** Balanced 30-fixture test suite — 20 living organisms (8 plants/trees, 6 birds, 6 insects/fungi) + 10 refusal cases (6 non-organisms, 4 people) for rigorous taxonomic and boundary validation.
- **D-15:** Production quality & build audit — Full verification suite: TypeScript check (`tsc --noEmit`), `fallow` dead-code remediation, Next.js production build (`pnpm build`), and CLI eval assert script.
- **D-16:** Outdoor field verification protocol — Comprehensive field walkthrough protocol (walk -> capture -> identification -> chime/haptic -> journal -> export) + submission summary and demo documentation.

### the agent's Discretion
- Exact oscillator frequencies and Q filter resonance for Cuelume chimes.
- SVG letter-spacing and viewBox calculation for Tegaki text sizing across mobile screens.
- Inline banner phrasing for denied camera/microphone permissions.

</decisions>

<canonical_refs>
## Canonical References

**Downstream agents MUST read these before planning or implementing.**

### Architecture & Requirements
- `DECISIONS.md` § Decisions 1, 2, 7, 8 — Local-first client architecture, Canvas EXIF stripping, and private IndexedDB storage
- `PRD.md` § 4.1, § 4.2, § 4.9, § 5.1 — Consent gate, storage persistence, evaluation harness, and design specifications
- `.planning/ROADMAP.md` § Phase 6 — Phase 6 scope, dependencies, requirements (`DSGN-03, DSGN-04, DSGN-05, CONS-01 to CONS-04, EVAL-01`), and success criteria
- `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md` § Consent, Design, Infrastructure — Specific acceptance criteria for consent, motion, sound, and evaluation

### Prior Phase Context & Schemas
- `.planning/phases/01-foundation-theme-day-1-verification-spikes/01-CONTEXT.md` — Tangerin Dream theme tokens, base Dexie tables, and evaluation fixture structure
- `.planning/phases/05-collection-journal-export/05-CONTEXT.md` — Settings preferences, storage persistence, and hunt celebration integration
- `lib/db.ts` — Dexie schemas for `settings`, `walks`, `entries`, and `notes`
- `components/consent/consent-modal.tsx` — Existing consent modal component and copy
- `app/(dev)/eval/page.tsx` & `app/api/eval/run/route.ts` — Benchmark runner and fixture schema

</canonical_refs>

<code_context>
## Existing Code Insights

### Reusable Assets
- `components/consent/consent-modal.tsx`: Existing Base UI Dialog consent implementation ready for strict modal gating and persistence status hookup.
- `hooks/use-consent.ts`: Hook for querying and recording consent version in `db.settings`.
- `components/ui/dialog.tsx`, `components/ui/card.tsx`, `components/ui/badge.tsx`, `components/ui/button.tsx`: Base UI primitives styled with Tangerin Dream theme tokens.
- `components/motion/motion-view.tsx`: Reduced-motion and visibility-aware animation wrapper.
- `app/(dev)/eval/page.tsx`: Existing 30-fixture visual benchmark dashboard.

- `lib/hunt.ts`: Daily hunt engine ready for completion sound and haptic triggers.
- `components/hunt/daily-hunt-celebration-dialog.tsx`: Hunt victory modal where Cuelume celebration chime and double haptic pulse integrate.
- `components/walk/candidate-picker-sheet.tsx`: Specimen confirmation sheet where Cuelume capture chime and haptic feedback integrate.
- `app/settings/page.tsx`: User settings page containing existing toggles for audio chimes and haptics.

### Established Patterns
- Client-side storage and settings via Dexie `db.settings`.
- Accessible dialogs using `@base-ui-components/react`.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` compliance across all CSS and JavaScript animations.
- Safe browser API degradation (`navigator.vibrate`, `window.AudioContext`, `navigator.storage.persist`).

### Integration Points
- `components/motion/tegaki-text.tsx`: New component providing SVG stroke dashoffset progressive reveal with Caveat font fallback.
- `lib/audio/cuelume.ts`: New Web Audio synthesizer module exposing `playCaptureChime()` and `playHuntChime()` with user preference gating.
- `lib/haptics.ts` (or `lib/audio/cuelume.ts`): Unified haptics trigger wrapping `navigator.vibrate` with settings check.
- `scripts/run-eval-suite.ts`: Headless CLI evaluation assert script testing all 30 fixtures with pass/fail thresholds.
- `app/entry/[id]/page.tsx` & `components/entry/fact-card.tsx`: Integrate `TegakiText` for confirmed species headers.

- Tegaki text uses SVG stroke dashoffset animation (~1.2s duration) with Google Font Caveat cursive fallback, resolving immediately to static text if `prefers-reduced-motion` is set.
- Cuelume chimes are synthesized entirely on the fly via Web Audio `OscillatorNode` and `GainNode`, producing dual-tone field bell chords without downloading audio files.
- Haptics provide a crisp 25ms tick on capture/selection and a double pulse [40ms, 60ms, 80ms] on confirmation and hunt completion.
- Consent modal completely prevents bypassing to `/walk` or hardware features on first launch until accepted.
- Evaluation runner can be triggered both from `/eval` and via CLI script (`pnpm test:eval`) with automated threshold assertions (≥70% accuracy, ≥90% refusal).
- Submission bundle includes an end-to-end outdoor field walkthrough verification protocol and updated documentation.

</specifics>

# Phase 6: Polish, Consent Gate, Evaluation & Submission - Research

**Date:** 2026-10-08
**Status:** Complete

## User Constraints (from CONTEXT.md)

### Locked Decisions
- **D-01:** SVG path stroke dashoffset / cursive draw — Organic pen stroke drawing effect revealing handwritten letter paths progressively over ~1.2s.
- **D-02:** Accessible font fallback & reduced motion — Google Font Caveat cursive fallback with instant opacity reveal when `prefers-reduced-motion` is active.
- **D-03:** Strategic lifecycle placement — Animated on Landing hero headline and Entry Fact Card confirmed specimen titles; plays once on view entrance without re-animating on incidental re-renders.
- **D-04:** Dynamic text rendering — SVG text stroke with dashoffset reveal combined with Google Font Caveat cursive styling to scale seamlessly to arbitrary Latin and binomial species names from Wikipedia.
- **D-05:** Organic acoustic synthesis — Dual-sine / triangle warm chime with exponential decay envelope (gentle brass/field bell character) using native Web Audio oscillators without external audio assets.
- **D-06:** Dual chime interaction mapping — Specimen confirmation triggers a warm major-third dual chime (E5–G#5); Daily Hunt completion triggers a joyful 4-note ascending arpeggio (C5–E5–G5–C6).
- **D-07:** Native tactile vibration pair — Crisp single tap [25ms] on capture/candidate selection, and resonant double pulse [40ms, 60ms, 80ms] on confirmation and daily hunt completion via `navigator.vibrate`.
- **D-08:** AudioContext lifecycle & preferences — Audio chimes defaulted to OFF; haptics defaulted to ON; lazy `AudioContext` resume on first user interaction to comply with mobile browser autoplay policies; configurable via `/settings`.
- **D-09:** App-wide blocking modal overlay — Strict full-screen modal on first visit; blocks interaction until accepted, storing version in IndexedDB and calling `navigator.storage.persist()`.
- **D-10:** Semver versioning & revocation — Semver string (`"1.0.0"`) and ISO timestamp stored in `db.settings`; re-prompts only on breaking policy bumps; revocable via Danger Zone reset in `/settings`.
- **D-11:** Non-blocking permission fallbacks — Non-blocking inline banner with helpful guidance + immediate manual fallback (e.g. file picker for photo, manual text note for voice) when hardware permissions are denied.
- **D-12:** Persistent storage status reporting — Silent request on consent acceptance; live status badge in `/settings` ('Durable / Best-effort') with a one-tap retry button.
- **D-13:** Dual evaluation runner — Interactive visual dashboard on `/eval` + headless CLI test script (`scripts/run-eval-suite.ts` / `pnpm test:eval`) asserting ≥70% accuracy and ≥90% refusal.
- **D-14:** Balanced 30-fixture test suite — 20 living organisms (8 plants/trees, 6 birds, 6 insects/fungi) + 10 refusal cases (6 non-organisms, 4 people) for rigorous taxonomic and boundary validation.
- **D-15:** Production quality & build audit — Full verification suite: TypeScript check (`tsc --noEmit`), `fallow` dead-code remediation, Next.js production build (`pnpm build`), and CLI eval assert script.
- **D-16:** Outdoor field verification protocol — Comprehensive field walkthrough protocol (walk -> capture -> identification -> chime/haptic -> journal -> export) + submission summary and demo documentation.

### the agent's Discretion
- Exact oscillator frequencies and Q filter resonance for Cuelume chimes.
- SVG letter-spacing and viewBox calculation for Tegaki text sizing across mobile screens.
- Inline banner phrasing for denied camera/microphone permissions.

### Deferred Ideas
- None — discussion stayed strictly within Phase 6 scope.

---

## Standard Stack

| Layer | Library / Tool | Version / Source | Purpose | Provenance |
|-------|---------------|------------------|---------|------------|
| Handwriting Font | Google Font `Caveat` | `next/font/google` | Cursive natural handwriting fallback token | [VERIFIED: next/font] |
| Animation | `motion/react` & SVG | `^12.4.7` | Stroke reveal, clip path wipes, reduced motion bypass | [VERIFIED: package.json:34] |
| Web Audio | Native `AudioContext` | W3C Standard | Synthesized UI audio chimes without audio files | [VERIFIED: MDN Web Audio API] |
| Haptics | `navigator.vibrate` | W3C Standard | Micro-vibration tactile feedback on supported devices | [VERIFIED: MDN Vibration API] |
| Data Layer | Dexie.js | `^4.0.11` | Client settings (`db.settings`) persistence & versioning | [VERIFIED: package.json:28] |
| Code Quality | `fallow` | CLI | Dead code remediation and unused export checking | [VERIFIED: user_rules] |
| Build & Types | `tsc`, Next.js | Next 16.4 | Typecheck and production bundle build | [VERIFIED: package.json:42] |

---

## Architecture Patterns

### Pattern 1: Tegaki Handwriting Animation (`components/motion/tegaki-text.tsx`)
Because species names are arbitrary and dynamic from Wikipedia, letter vectors cannot be pre-drawn manually. The solution combines Google Font `Caveat` loaded via `next/font/google` with a dual-layer SVG or clip-path motion unmasking:
1. `app/layout.tsx` imports `Caveat({ subsets: ['latin'], variable: '--font-handwriting', display: 'swap' })`.
2. `components/motion/tegaki-text.tsx` renders an SVG text element or motion container with `font-handwriting`.
3. Animated stroke dashoffset + clip-path linear reveal sweeps left-to-right over 1.2s, mimicking pen-ink flow.
4. Hook `useReducedMotion()` inspects `prefers-reduced-motion`. If true, animation duration is 0ms, rendering instant static text.
5. Employs `useRef(false)` to ensure animation runs only on view entrance, avoiding replays during re-renders.

### Pattern 2: Cuelume Web Audio Synthesis (`lib/audio/cuelume.ts`)
Synthesizes gentle outdoor chimes purely with browser oscillators:
1. **Lazy Initialization**: Browser autoplay policies require an explicit user gesture before resuming an `AudioContext`. `getAudioContext()` checks `typeof window !== 'undefined'`, creates/reuses `AudioContext`, and calls `.resume()`.
2. **Specimen Confirmation Chime**:
   - Chords: Major third (E5: 659.25 Hz + G#5: 830.61 Hz).
   - Oscillators: Dual `sine` and soft `triangle` with 30ms offset.
   - Envelope: Exponential gain ramp from 0.15 to 0.0001 over 0.8s.
3. **Daily Hunt Celebration Chime**:
   - 4-note ascending arpeggio: C5 (523.25 Hz) → E5 (659.25 Hz) → G5 (783.99 Hz) → C6 (1046.50 Hz) at 120ms intervals.
   - Envelope: 0.6s decay per note.
4. **Preference Check**: Queries `db.settings` `'user_settings'`. If `soundEnabled` is false, exits silently.

### Pattern 3: Tactile Haptic Pulses (`lib/haptics.ts`)
1. Checks `'vibrate' in navigator` and verifies `hapticsEnabled` in `db.settings`.
2. `triggerCaptureHaptic()`: single 25ms tick.
3. `triggerConfirmHaptic()` / `triggerHuntWinHaptic()`: resonant double pulse `[40, 60, 80]` ms.

### Pattern 4: Global Consent Gate Verification
1. `components/consent/consent-modal.tsx` is mounted globally in `app/layout.tsx`.
2. Uses Base UI `<Dialog open={!hasConsented}>` with `disablePointerDismissal={true}` and `hideCloseButton={true}`.
3. Upon acceptance:
   - Sets `db.settings.put({ id: 'consent', version: '1.0.0', acceptedAt: new Date().toISOString() })`.
   - Calls `navigator.storage.persist()`.
4. `/settings` provides live persistence status display (`Persisted` vs `Best Effort`) with manual re-request.
5. In addition, `/walk` guards active tracking and capture if unconsented.

### Pattern 5: 30-Fixture Evaluation Suite & Headless CLI Runner
1. `public/eval-fixtures/fixtures.json` structured as 20 organisms (8 plants, 6 birds, 6 insects) + 10 refusals (6 non-organisms, 4 people).
2. `scripts/run-eval-suite.ts` loads fixtures and runs them against Google Generative AI (if `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY` is present) or the high-fidelity mock engine matching `/api/eval/run/route.ts`.
3. Verifies benchmark criteria:
   - Accuracy ≥ 70%
   - Refusal Rate ≥ 90%
4. Exits with exit code 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL.
5. Script added to `package.json` as `"test:eval": "tsx scripts/run-eval-suite.ts"`.

---

## Don't Hand-Roll

- **Don't Hand-Roll Audio Files**: Do NOT bundle `.mp3` or `.wav` sound effects. Web Audio API oscillators are zero-bandwidth, seek-safe, and load instantaneously.
- **Don't Hand-Roll Font Loaders**: Use `next/font/google` for `Caveat` font loading; it automatically optimizes, self-hosts, and avoids layout shifts.
- **Don't Hand-Roll Haptic Fallbacks**: If `navigator.vibrate` is absent (iOS Safari or desktop), silently swallow without errors.
- **Don't Hand-Roll Modals**: Use existing `@base-ui-components/react` dialog primitives with Tangerin Dream tokens.

---

## Common Pitfalls

1. **AudioContext Autoplay Blocking**:
   *Pitfall*: Calling `new AudioContext()` at module top-level triggers browser console warnings and fails to play audio until resumed by user interaction.
   *Fix*: Instantiate lazily inside `getAudioContext()` and invoke only inside user gesture handlers (click/tap).
2. **Reduced Motion Violations**:
   *Pitfall*: Drawing animations that ignore user accessibility preferences.
   *Fix*: Check `useReducedMotion()`. If active, render static text with 0ms transition.
3. **SVG Font Metrics & Text Clipping**:
   *Pitfall*: Fixed width SVG causing species names with varying lengths to truncate or overflow.
   *Fix*: Render text with CSS responsive units or motion mask wrapper with dynamic text sizing.
4. **Fixture Discrepancies**:
   *Pitfall*: Running eval with unmatched categories causing false negative metrics.
   *Fix*: Standardize `public/eval-fixtures/fixtures.json` to exactly 20 organisms and 10 negative refusal cases.

---

## Validation Architecture

### Verification Commands
1. `pnpm tsc --noEmit` — Type-check passes with 0 errors.
2. `pnpm test:eval` — 30-fixture batch evaluation passes with ≥70% accuracy and ≥90% refusal.
3. `pnpm build` — Next.js 16 production build compiles cleanly without errors.
4. `pnpm test:all` or individual spike/unit test execution.
5. Outdoor Field Walkthrough Checklist verified.

278: ## 9.5. UI-Consideration Probe (post-verification)
279: 
280: Run AFTER the checker approves the UI-SPEC (VERIFIED, or force-approved at step 9) — never inline
281: during authoring, so a revision-loop researcher rewrite (step 9) cannot clobber the section and the
282: `## UI Considerations` block is committed with the FINAL UI-SPEC. This is the visual analog of
283: spec-phase Step 5.5's edge probe, retargeted to the UI element/state axis. Reference:
284: @~/.gemini/antigravity/gsd-core/references/ui-consideration-probe.md.
285: 
286: **Skip conditions:** if `--auto` and the UI-SPEC already carries a resolved `## UI Considerations`
287: section (re-run), the write-back is idempotent (it REPLACES that section, never appends). If the
288: runtime is non-the agent and the probe engine cannot be resolved, the shim FAILS LOUD (below) — it
289: never silently no-ops (a silent skip would drop the whole state-coverage axis).
290: 
291: **Runtime coverage compute — resolve and invoke ui-consideration-probe.cjs:**
292: 
293: ```bash
294: # Resolve the compiled ui-consideration-probe.cjs against the GSD install dir via RUNTIME_DIR
295: # (#448) — NOT the consuming project's git root — falling back to git toplevel / $HOME/.gemini/antigravity.
296: # Mirrors spec-phase.md Step 5.5's edge-probe resolution idiom verbatim (same candidate paths).
297: _GSD_RT="${RUNTIME_DIR:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)}"
298: UI_PROBE_JS=$(for _c in \
299:   "$_GSD_RT/gsd-core/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
300:   "$_GSD_RT/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
301:   "$_GSD_RT/.agents/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
302:   "$HOME/.gemini/antigravity/gsd-core/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
303:   "$HOME/.gemini/antigravity/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs"; do
304:   [ -f "$_c" ] && { echo "$_c"; break; }
305: done)
306: 
307: # Graceful degradation — never a silent skip. Build ONLY when $_GSD_RT is a verified GSD source
308: # checkout (has tsconfig.build.json + src/ui-consideration-probe.cts), pinned with --prefix so we
309: # never trigger the CONSUMING project's own build during a ui-phase. Real installs ship the
310: # compiled .cjs via prepublishOnly, so this path only matters in a GSD dev checkout.
311: if [ -z "$UI_PROBE_JS" ]; then
312:   if [ -f "$_GSD_RT/tsconfig.build.json" ] && [ -f "$_GSD_RT/src/ui-consideration-probe.cts" ]; then
313:     npm --prefix "$_GSD_RT" run build:lib 2>/dev/null || true
314:     UI_PROBE_JS=$(for _c in \
315:       "$_GSD_RT/gsd-core/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
316:       "$_GSD_RT/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
317:       "$_GSD_RT/.agents/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
318:       "$HOME/.gemini/antigravity/gsd-core/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
319:       "$HOME/.gemini/antigravity/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs"; do
320:       [ -f "$_c" ] && { echo "$_c"; break; }
321:     done)
322:   fi
323:   if [ -z "$UI_PROBE_JS" ]; then
324:     echo "ERROR: ui-consideration-probe.cjs not found — reinstall GSD or run \`npm run build:lib\` in your GSD checkout." >&2
325:     exit 1
326:   fi
327: fi
328: 
329: # Element extraction (MANUAL BY DESIGN — not an oversight): the agent reads the researcher-authored
330: # UI-SPEC prose (the described surfaces — the Design System / Copywriting rows and any element the
331: # researcher named) and writes ONE object per UI element/surface: {"id","text"} where text is the
332: # prose describing it. This mirrors spec-phase Step 5.5's edge-probe REQS_JSON step VERBATIM — a
333: # hand-populated heredoc guarded by the fail-loud <replace:> check below — the established, shipped
334: # pattern for feeding a probe from a prose spec. It is NOT mechanized on purpose: a UI-SPEC has no
335: # single machine-parseable "elements" column — surfaces are distributed across design-token tables
336: # (Design System / Typography / Color), the Copywriting section, and prose the researcher names, so a
337: # regex/table parse would fail-OPEN (miss a prose-named surface, or feed a design-token row as a bogus
338: # element). The agent-authored heredoc + fail-loud guard is the conservative choice, identical to the
339: # requirement-side edge-probe path (RR-04). If a future UI-SPEC gains a canonical element table,
340: # revisit to parse it. Populate the heredoc from the UI-SPEC; the guard below fails loud on a
341: # forgotten substitution (never a no-op).
342: ELEMENTS_JSON=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ui-probe-elements-XXXXXX") && mv "$ELEMENTS_JSON" "${ELEMENTS_JSON}.json" && ELEMENTS_JSON="${ELEMENTS_JSON}.json" || exit 1
343: cat > "$ELEMENTS_JSON" <<'JSON'
344: [
345:   { "id": "E1", "text": "<replace: element/surface description from the UI-SPEC prose>" }
346: ]
347: JSON
348: if ! node -e 'const a=require(process.argv[1]);if(!Array.isArray(a)||a.length===0)process.exit(1);if(a.some(e=>typeof e.text!=="string"||!e.text.trim()||e.text.includes("<replace:")))process.exit(1)' "$ELEMENTS_JSON" 2>/dev/null; then
349:   rm -f "$ELEMENTS_JSON"
350:   echo "ERROR: ui-probe elements JSON is empty/invalid or still holds the <replace: …> placeholder — populate \$ELEMENTS_JSON from the UI-SPEC's described surfaces before this step runs." >&2
351:   exit 1
352: fi
353: # Invoke the compiled engine and CAPTURE its report. FATAL-INVOKE GUARD: use `if ! COVERAGE=$(…)`,
354: # NEVER a bare `COVERAGE=$(node …)` — a bare capture swallows the engine's exit 2 (invalid shape /
355: # bad input) and falls through to prose re-derivation: fail-OPEN at the exact boundary the engine
356: # validation protects.
357: if ! COVERAGE=$(node "$UI_PROBE_JS" "$ELEMENTS_JSON"); then
358:   rm -f "$ELEMENTS_JSON"
359:   echo "ERROR: ui-consideration-probe engine failed (invalid shapes or bad input) — fix the element(s) and re-run; never proceed with empty coverage." >&2
360:   exit 1
361: fi
362: rm -f "$ELEMENTS_JSON"
363: # Malformed-report guard: exit 0 but garbage. The report must parse as { items[], coverage{} }.
364: if ! printf '%s' "$COVERAGE" | node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>{let r;try{r=JSON.parse(s)}catch{process.exit(1)}if(!r||!Array.isArray(r.items)||typeof r.coverage!=="object"||r.coverage===null)process.exit(1)})'; then
365:   echo "ERROR: ui-consideration-probe produced an unparseable or malformed coverage report — refusing to proceed with the resolution loop." >&2
366:   exit 1
367: fi
368: # Zero-applicable guard: a report where NO category applied across ANY element is far more likely a
369: # classification miss (or malformed elements) than a genuinely state-free UI. Surface it loudly.
370: APPLICABLE=$(printf '%s' "$COVERAGE" | node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>{let n=0;try{n=JSON.parse(s).coverage.applicable}catch{n=0}process.stdout.write(String(n))})')
371: if [ "$APPLICABLE" = "0" ]; then
372:   echo "WARNING: ui-consideration-probe proposed ZERO applicable categories across all elements — likely a classification miss or malformed elements, not a genuinely state-free UI. Do NOT silently write an empty UI Considerations section." >&2
373: fi
374: ```
375: 
376: If `$APPLICABLE` is `0`, do NOT proceed silently: ask via AskUserQuestion ("The UI probe found no
377: applicable state considerations — is this genuinely a state-free surface, or should we revisit the
378: element descriptions?"). Only write an empty section after explicit confirmation.
379: 
380: **Propose-then-confirm (the partial-cue mitigation — load-bearing).** For each element, the engine
381: reports the DETECTED element kinds (`classifyElement` over the built `.cjs`). The prose classifier
382: is heuristic and LOSSY: a surface that is genuinely both a form and a list, but whose prose trips
383: only the form cue, under-covers — and because SOMETHING classified, no `unclassified` signal fires.
384: So SURFACE the detected kinds to the user (AskUserQuestion) and ask whether any real element kind
385: was missed. If the user ADDs a kind, re-run that element with an authored `elements` override
386: (the union of detected + added) so the missed categories are raised. A single tripped cue is a
387: SIGNAL, not proof the element is only that kind — the confirm step, not the heuristic, is what makes
388: coverage sound.
389: 
390: **Resolution loop** (mirror spec-phase 5.5): resolve each applicable consideration via
391: AskUserQuestion — **Specify** (→ `resolved`, verification: explicit; write a concrete truth) / **Dismiss (reason required)** /
392: **Backstop** (→ `resolved`, verification: backstop; a held-out/visual UI-state test) / **Defer** (→ `unresolved`). An `unclassified` row is
393: a manual-review nudge, not a hard block. Text mode (`workflow.text_mode` / `--text`) → numbered lists.
394: 
395: **Kind-confirmation under `--auto`.** The propose-then-confirm step above is an AskUserQuestion, so
396: under `--auto` it follows the spec-phase 5.5 convention (replace AskUserQuestion with the agent's
397: recommended choice): the agent re-reads each element's prose and authors the `elements` override (the
398: union of the detected kinds + any kind it identifies as missed) instead of prompting — so `--auto`
399: recall rests on the agent's kind-identification, not the heuristic cue-match alone. This matters because
400: `autoResolve` (below) is a RESOLUTION floor only: it resolves the *detected* categories and cannot
401: recover a kind that was never surfaced, so recall is fixed HERE, at kind-confirmation, before
402: resolution runs.
403: 
404: **`--auto` mode (two layers).** The adapter's `autoResolve` is the CODE floor: every applicable
405: consideration auto-resolves with `verification: backstop` (carrying the taxonomy question as its
406: resolution) and an `unclassified` candidate stays `unresolved` — it NEVER auto-`dismiss`es and never
407: auto-resolves an unclassified item with backstop (#1110). On top of that floor the workflow MAY
408: upgrade an item to `resolved` (verification: explicit) when a
409: defensible acceptance criterion can be written (the same judgment spec-phase 5.5 applies in prose).
410: An auto `--auto` run therefore leaves un-upgraded items as `resolved` (verification: backstop): at verify time each one
411: with no wired evidence routes to `insufficient_spec → human_needed` — never a silent pass (#1154).
412: That surfacing is the intended honest-verifier behavior, not over-flagging.
413: 
414: **Write-back.** Populate a `## UI Considerations` section in the UI-SPEC from the resolved
415: considerations, in the format the shipped plan-phase `## UI Considerations` lift rule reads:
416: `resolved` (explicit) → a truth string; `resolved` (backstop) → a flat scalar `{ statement, verification: backstop }`;
417: `unresolved` → an explicit `⚠ unresolved — planner must treat as assumption` row. Empty-state and
418: error-state COPY stays in `## Copywriting Contract` — the considerations section covers shape-rooted
419: STATE coverage and REFERENCES those rows rather than restating the copy (de-dup). IDEMPOTENT: if a
420: `## UI Considerations` section already exists, REPLACE it — never append a duplicate.

Declared values (multiples of 4):

|-------|-------|-------|

| Role | Value | Usage |

| Accent (10%) | `#F35C2B` (Terracotta) | Primary CTA buttons, Tegaki pen strokes, active toggles, badge borders |
| Destructive | `#DC2626` | Danger Zone data wipe confirmation |

Accent reserved for: Primary action buttons (`I Understand & Accept`, `Run Batch Evaluation`), active settings toggle thumbs, Tegaki handwriting pen stroke highlights, and verified taxonomic badges.

---

## Copywriting Contract

| Element | Copy |
|---------|------|
| Consent Gate Modal Title | "Welcome to Treads" |
| Consent Gate Primary CTA | "I Understand & Accept" |
| Consent Gate Subtext | "Field journal, species records, high-res photos, and notes remain strictly in your browser's IndexedDB." |
| Permission Denied Banner (Camera) | "Camera access was denied. You can still upload photos from your device files." |
| Permission Denied Banner (Mic) | "Microphone access was denied. You can still type observation notes manually." |
| Permission Denied Banner (GPS) | "Location access was denied. Free-form walking is active without path recording." |
| Storage Persist Granted Badge | "Durable Storage: Protected" |
| Storage Persist Best-Effort Badge | "Durable Storage: Best-effort" |
| Storage Persist Action | "Protect Storage" |
| Tegaki Hero Tagline | "Step outside. Notice what lives." |

| Autoplay policy | `Cuelume` Web Audio | ✅ covered | AudioContext initialized/resumed only on explicit user click/tap, avoiding browser console autoplay warnings. |
